facts.text: I've been having pain in my side, in the flank area.
It comes and goes.
It's been going on for 5 months.
I've had five urinary tract infections over the past 2 years.
I haven't noticed any change in my peeing, like going more often or more urgently, except when I have a UTI.
I haven't had any fever recently.
I haven't had any nausea.
I haven't been vomiting.
I haven't had any rash.
I haven't had any joint pain.
Apart from the UTIs, I haven't had any infections recently.
I haven't lost any significant weight.
I haven't gained any significant weight.
I don't have any significant medical problems.
As far as I know, I've never had kidney stones.
As far as I know, no one in my family has kidney disease.
I don't smoke.
I drink alcohol socially.
I work in IT management.
I haven't travelled recently.
I don't have any unusual eating habits.

findings.name: abdominal examination
findings.result: Inspection: no visible abnormalities or distension; auscultation: normal bowel sounds; percussion: no shifting dullness, no flank pain elicited; palpation: nontender upper abdominal masses felt bilaterally.

findings.name: basic metabolic panel
findings.result: Blood urea nitrogen 29 mg/dL (elevated); creatinine 1.4 mg/dL (elevated).

findings.name: renal ultrasound
findings.result: Bilaterally enlarged kidneys with multiple parenchymal anechoic masses.

f001: The side of the flank pain is not stated (the abdominal masses are bilateral); the text keeps it unspecified.
f015: 'as per patient's knowledge' is read as covering both kidney stones and familial kidney disease.

x005.source_text: No visible abnormalities or distension. + Normal bowel sounds. + No shifting dullness or flank pain elicited. + Nontender upper abdominal masses felt bilaterally.

x007.source_text: Bilaterally enlarged kidneys with multiple parenchymal anechoic masses.

x002: The blood pressure also appears under Test_Results.Blood_Work with the interpretation '(indication of hypertension)'; both leaves are merged into the vital record and the interpretation is dropped.
x006: Only BUN and creatinine are reported; the record is named as the panel they belong to.

leakage.reason: 'kidney' is a gold-diagnosis word; here it is the organ in a source denial of kidney stones, not the diagnosis.
'kidney' is a gold-diagnosis word; the fact is the source's denial of familial kidney disease (as far as she knows), which does not name the diagnosis.

source_issues: Blood pressure 150/88 mmHg is listed twice: as a vital sign and under Test_Results.Blood_Work with an interpretation.
Secondary_Symptoms holds denials and history ('No nausea or vomiting', 'No significant change in urinary habits', 'History of multiple UTIs'); merged with the same statements in the History.
No family history of kidney disease is reported for an autosomal dominant disease ('as per patient's knowledge').
notes: The urinary-habits sentence is one statement with examples (frequency, urgency) and an exception (during a UTI), so it is one fact with the examples as aliases.
Finding aliases avoid the word 'kidney' to keep gold words out of request names; 'renal ultrasound' is the clinical name.

extras.objective_for_doctor: Evaluate and diagnose the patient presenting with chronic flank pain and a history of urinary tract infections.
